executiveSummary: GM1728 passes the full deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, headline demography, 25 neighbourhoods, five BAG places, 19 BRT settlements, two NWB-derived logical links, null semantics, local reconciliation, causal ledgers and exact zero-intensity behavior are coherent. Release remains correction-required for two related high-severity spatial defects. The named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset assigns Bladel direct municipality-wide inundation stress of 1.7634 from T+12 through T+72, despite both the current Brabant-Zuidoost risk profile and Bladel's official climate stress test excluding direct primary/regional-defence flooding here; the credible local mechanisms are Groote Beerze/Dalems Stroompje water, groundwater, extreme rain and indirect blocked drainage. It yields 12,638 modeled people under pressure and 759,887 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours at T+72. Separately, storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire use the identical exact neighbourhood order. A focused synthetic source at Ten Vorsel leaves its containing Verspreide huizen Bladel neighbourhood 15th of 25 while two neighbourhoods 6.7–7.3 km away rank first and second. This conflicts with source-aware use in the locally documented Cartierheide, Neterselse Heide and southern-forest fire landscape. Public context usefully exposes 127 De Dommel weirs, three sewer pumps, RWZI Hapert, provider responsibility, eleven education locations, external acute hospitals and current road observations, but none supplies operational topology or causally changes the simulation. Physical Enexis, Brabant Water, sewer, telecom, care, supply, emergency-access, Belgian mutual-aid and restoration data remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 and Gemeente gegeneraliseerd 2025 — GM1728
supports: Machine-readable official-context identity and annual statistics: GM1728/Bladel, 21,006 residents, density 279 per square kilometre, 5,061 residents aged 65 or older and 2,914 one-person households.

The companion annual generalized municipality and neighbourhood polygons at https://api.pdok.nl/cbs/gebiedsindelingen/ogc/v1 are CC BY 4.0 and provide the administrative geometry consumed by the application.
CBS rounded or suppressed neighbourhood values require explicit null and reconciliation semantics; administrative boundaries are not hazard, catchment, provider or incident footprints.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, definitief versie 1.0
supports: Bladel is one of the 21 municipalities in Brabant-Zuidoost. The profile says the region's relatively high position means there is no direct flood danger; large-river flooding to the north can instead block drainage from southern Brabant.

The regional all-hazard analysis covers high river water, extreme precipitation, defence failure, wildfire, winter weather, heat, storm, electricity, gas/heat, telecom, drinking water, wastewater, cyberattack and cascading vital-process dependencies.

Wildfire behavior depends on vegetation, management, weather, extinguishing-water availability, access and location; A67 and provincial routes crossing nature are vulnerable, smoke can travel beyond the fire and electricity infrastructure can cascade.

It states that Brabant Water has high redundancy, that normal drinking-water failures are usually repaired within hours, that prolonged gas consequences depend strongly on winter conditions, and that hospitals, public-safety sites and telecom depend on power.
The strategic profile is static four-year risk context, not a live warning, local footprint, asset state, probability feed or GM1728 restoration estimate; no explicit dataset reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Bladel / Provincie Noord-Brabant climate-adaptation portal
evidenceSources.title: Klimaatstresstest gemeente Bladel
supports: The official local study used sewer models, infrared images, public data and local knowledge, and publishes separate mapped appendices for rainwater, water-system flooding, drought, surface temperature and heat stress for Bladel and its five centres.

It calculates no inundation from primary or regional defences in either the current climate or WH2050; water-system flood risk instead increases chiefly in the Groote Beerze and Dalems Stroompje valleys.

It identifies Cartierheide, Natuurreservaat De Goorloop, Kroonvensche Heide and Neterselse Heide as drought-sensitive, and Cartierheide, Neterselse Heide and southern forests as vulnerable to drought and fire.
Bladel lies on relatively high sandy ground with deep groundwater and often-dry watercourses; the 2018 Hapert pond dried with fish mortality and extreme rainfall in June 2016 caused many complaints.
The analysis projects more intense rain, greater precipitation deficit, more tropical days and longer periods of warm nights; local heat differences depend on vegetation and paved surface.
This is authoritative scenario/context mapping, not an observed current event or machine-ready operational layer. The portal states no fixed refresh cadence or explicit native-GIS reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Zuidoost / Gemeenten De Kempen / Staatsbosbeheer
evidenceSources.title: Stap vooruit in beheersing natuurbranden in de Kempen
supports: Bladel, Bergeijk, Eersel and Reusel-De Mierden signed a joint De Kempen wildfire-management plan with VRBZO and Staatsbosbeheer.

Named measures include replacing conifers with deciduous trees, wetting nature areas and improving emergency-service access, demonstrating that fuel, moisture and access are spatial determinants rather than a municipality-wide random rank.
The page and plan announcement provide official preparedness context, not an ignition perimeter, real-time fuel moisture, response capacity, fixed update feed or documented reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap De Dommel / Het Waterschapshuis via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Groote Beerze, RWZI Hapert and IMWA/DAMO machine-readable water context
evidenceSources.edition: current project page and application snapshot retrieved 2026-09-02
supports: The Dalemstroompje and Aa/Goorloop meet south of N284 between Bladel and Hapert to form the Groote Beerze, which runs between Casteren and Netersel. De Dommel is redesigning this catchment to retain water in drought and create room during heavy rain.

The companion RWZI page at https://www.dommel.nl/rioolwaterzuivering-hapert states that RWZI Hapert treats wastewater for Bladel and Reusel-De Mierden, about 12,200 cubic metres daily and up to 60,000 cubic metres per day during extreme rain.

The current HWH OGC snapshot from https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 contains 127 realized De Dommel weirs, three sewer pumps and RWZI Hapert inside the generalized GM1728 boundary.

HWH object APIs are CC BY-SA 4.0; Kunstwerken declares weekly updates, while contributor and collection completeness vary. Static object presence does not establish hydraulic connectivity, controls, live status, emergency power or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Crisisplan 2024–2027
supports: The plan explicitly treats a short acute crisis as lasting up to about three days and allows transition to a long-crisis structure, directly matching the simulator's first-72-hour focus.
Monitoring and signalering are continuous; acute threats can trigger CoPI or ROT and a planning staff develops a shared multidisciplinary picture.

General public-order and safety authority and functional-chain authority for electricity, food and other sectors remain distinct; VRBZO separately publishes coordination plans for energy, drinking water, water, telecom, rail and thematic cross-border cooperation with Belgium.

It defines roles and coordination, not deterministic intervention effects, staffing, stocks, service restoration times or a machine-readable incident feed; it follows the policy cycle and states no dataset reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Noord-Brabant / ProRail via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Nationaal Wegenbestand and N284 Reusel–Bladel–Hapert official transport context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB application snapshot 2026-08-01; official N284 pages accessed 2026-09-02

The provincial page at https://www.brabant.nl/onderwerpen/verkeer-vervoer/wegen-infraprojecten-brabant/n284-reusel-bladel-hapert/ says N284 runs Reusel–Bladel–Hapert and is the important connection toward Eindhoven and A67; Bladel's official mobility context says A67 connects the municipality with Antwerp, Veldhoven, Eindhoven and A2.
The companion ProRail OGC API at https://api.pdok.nl/prorail/spoorwegen/ogc/v1 is CC0 with manual updates; no station lies in GM1728.
Static geometry and nominal graph units do not establish live closure, congestion, transit operation, Belgian continuity, emergency access, evacuation throughput or utility capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu / DUO / KNMI / NDW / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting
evidenceSources.title: Official machine-readable care, education, weather, road-state and provider context
supports: RIVM's version 1.1 acute-care questionnaire, published 2026-07-03 under CC0 1.0 on an annual cycle, has no acute hospital in GM1728; nearest straight-line reference-point destinations are Máxima Medisch Centrum at 12.60 km and Catharina Ziekenhuis at 18.95 km, both reporting 24/7 emergency departments.

DUO RIO at https://onderwijsdata.duo.nl/dataset/c416acd1-e083-4ec6-9203-3b20f98fe143 is daily machine-readable CC BY context; eleven current registered education locations intersect GM1728, but none is thereby a shelter or staffed emergency facility.

KNMI five-minute radar at https://dataplatform.knmi.nl/dataset/access/radar-reflectivity-composites-2-0 is CC BY 4.0 observed context; NDW DATEX II current situations at https://opendata.ndw.nu/actueel_beeld.xml.gz are continuously published CC0-unless-stated road context. Neither is aligned to or causal for an arbitrary exercise clock.

Live public-domain provider WMS/WFS documented at https://wiki.service.mijnaansluiting.nl/wiki/spaces/Wiki/pages/693731329 returned Enexis for electricity/gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and Ziggo for fixed media at Bladel's reference point; drainage returned no polygon and coverage can be incomplete or overlapping.

These sources identify dated offer, registered use, observation, restriction and responsibility context, never live hospital acceptance, staffing, shelter designation, physical utility topology, coverage quality, switching, backup or restoration.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, monotonic cumulative burden, route bounds and local reconciliation pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1728 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 27.27 seconds on the final focused run.
Every canonical preset at intensity zero produces exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated frames are deterministic; state is finite and bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; and route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity.
All local maps preserve 21,006 allocated residents including exact zero for two zero-population neighbourhoods; maximum population/service reconciliation error was 1.42e-14.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The generic major-river field contradicts official Bladel evidence, while a shared neighbourhood seed ignores hazard mechanism and an explicit wildfire source.
notes: River inundation stress rises from zero at T+0 to 0.6207 at T+6 and 1.7634 at T+12, remaining 1.7634 through T+72; affected population is 10,869 at T+12, 12,053 at T+24 and 12,638 at T+48/T+72.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-461 measures GM1728's centre against three coarse diagonal corridors and lines 670-675 turn that screen into direct water. E02 and E03 both exclude direct flood danger from the relevant defences while retaining indirect and catchment-specific water pathways.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3404-3418 applies municipality severity through one scenario/neighbourhood hash. Severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack and wildfire therefore have the identical exact 25-neighbourhood order.

At T+24 those seven presets begin Verspreide huizen Netersel, Verspreide huizen Casteren, De Sleutel, Hapert Noord and Bladel Centrum. This is not derived from the Groote Beerze/Dalems Stroompje catchment, pavement/vegetation, power/telecom targets, roads or nature-fire fuel.

In a focused synthetic T+24 wildfire with source [5.223, 51.348] at Ten Vorsel, direct-fire intensity is 0.5832, smoke 0.5459 and municipality severity 0.5813. Yet the containing Verspreide huizen Bladel ranks 15/25 at 0.5307; Verspreide huizen Netersel 7.298 km away and Verspreide huizen Casteren 6.667 km away rank first and second. The source test is not evidence of an observed fire.

Canonical coastal direct inundation and remote-wildfire direct flame remain exactly zero; these correctly scoped zeros do not establish absence of indirect coastal supply effects or a local Bladel fire.

notes: River T+24 availability is power 0.4521, water 0.4472, drainage 0.3042, gas 0.7018, telecom 0.4566, mobility 0.3691, facilities 0.5345 and supply 0.3572.
Compound T+24 availability is power 0.4166, water 0.3867, drainage 0.3310, gas 0.5924, telecom 0.2343, mobility 0.5697, facilities 0.4812 and supply 0.3762.

The causal graph has no named Enexis feeder/station, Brabant Water pressure zone, sewer catchment/control, mobile network, RWZI dependency, hospital transfer, school/shelter, depot, supermarket stock or Belgian support node.

All eight service views reuse the same two road-derived links and nominal total 410; transferSemantics at packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:2066 remains logical-proxy and never physical utility topology.
The street utility detail adapter is explicitly Liander-only while Bladel's provider territory is Enexis, so it cannot fill the physical power/gas topology gap.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve scenario confidence, controls, dependency ordering and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, drivers, local vulnerability/demand factors, recovery progress and service-restoration counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness changes modeled people/supply consequences after physical pressure rather than changing physical hazard fragility.
Operational controls and time-gated interventions are labeled scenario assumptions; road-derived utility flows remain logical proxies.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure against a matched no-event baseline and are not observed outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water and response-delay safeguards behave consistently, but unsupported forcing and absent operational resources prevent local recovery interpretation.
notes: Unsupported river forcing remains active at T+72: pressure is 0.5670, 12,638 people remain under pressure and cumulative proxy burden reaches 759,887 person-hours.

River T+72 keeps power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility and supply at their T+24 values while facilities falls from 0.5345 to 0.3934 through generic dependencies; this is not an operator, hospital or municipality forecast.
Pluvial water clears by T+48 and pressure falls from 0.2448 at T+24 to 0.0529 at T+72; compound retains 0.3562 generic water and pressure rises from 0.5782 to 0.5929 through T+72.

The two-week heatwave retains 25.05 degrees Celsius and drought severity 0.5978 at T+72 while affectedPopulation is zero; this threshold outcome must not be read as no residual health, care or water-demand burden.

E06 defines flexible monitoring, an acute approximately three-day response and transition to long-crisis structures, but model interventions are not actual CoPI/ROT, municipal, water-board or operator decisions.
Actual water-control state, N284/A67/Belgian access, provider switching, hospitals, crews, mutual aid, fuel, spares, staff, stocks and restoration estimates are unknown.

findings.summary: A coarse proximity corridor creates unsupported sustained direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation across Bladel.
findings.evidence: E02 states that high-lying Brabant-Zuidoost has no direct flood danger and identifies only an indirect large-river mechanism in which northern flooding can block southern drainage. E03 independently calculates no flooding from primary or regional defences for Bladel in the current climate or WH2050, while naming Groote Beerze and Dalems Stroompje catchment pathways. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-461 nevertheless measures Bladel's centre against diagonal lines and lines 670-675 emit direct municipality water. The canonical preset reaches internal inundation stress 1.7634 at T+12 and holds it through T+72, with 12,053 modeled people/195,265 event-attributable essential-service person-hours at T+24 and 12,638/759,887 at T+72. No defence failure, connected footprint, backwater model, level, arrival, duration or local depth supports this result.
findings.action: Mark GM1728's named-major-river result unsupported/Unknown and make direct forcing numerically neutral until an expert-selected hydraulic footprint exists. Preserve Groote Beerze/Dalems Stroompje, groundwater, pluvial and indirect blocked-drainage mechanisms as unresolved rather than safe. The durable model must sample a named/versioned LIWO or De Dommel scenario and expose people/services only within its connected footprint.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated hazards reuse one exact neighbourhood rank instead of Bladel's mapped water, heat, network and land-cover mechanisms.
findings.evidence: E03 supplies separate official maps and mechanism distinctions for rainwater, water-system flooding, drought, surface temperature and heat stress. At T+24 the simulator gives severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack and wildfire the identical exact order of all 25 neighbourhoods, beginning Verspreide huizen Netersel, Verspreide huizen Casteren, De Sleutel, Hapert Noord and Bladel Centrum. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3404-3418 samples no stress-test cell, elevation, catchment, paving/vegetation, network target, road exposure or fuel. De Sleutel's high rank happens to align with a documented 2018 cloudburst, but the same rank cannot validate every other hazard.
findings.action: Label all current neighbourhood rankings synthetic/unsupported and prohibit deployment decisions from them. Obtain the native GIS behind E03 or its current successor; retain event definition, resolution, units, edition, no-data, validation and licence. Use separately versioned pluvial, water-system, heat and drought surfaces, and require exact rankings to differ when inputs differ.

findings.summary: An explicit source in Bladel's southern nature landscape does not control the neighbourhood map of direct fire impact.
findings.evidence: E03 identifies Cartierheide, Neterselse Heide and forests in southern Bladel as drought/fire vulnerable; E04 records fuel conversion, wetting and emergency-access measures for De Kempen. In a reproducible synthetic T+24 test, a source at Ten Vorsel [5.223, 51.348] gives direct-fire intensity 0.5832, smoke 0.5459 and municipality severity 0.5813. Yet containing Verspreide huizen Bladel ranks 15/25 at hazard 0.5307, below Verspreide huizen Netersel 7.298 km away and Verspreide huizen Casteren 6.667 km away. This proves local allocation ignores the selected source; it is not evidence of an actual fire.
findings.action: Until source/perimeter-aware allocation exists, mark neighbourhood flame ranks unsupported and do not use them for dispatch. Prefer an authorized NIPV Risiko-index Natuurbranden export; otherwise combine BRT TOP10NL eligible land cover, an explicit ignition/perimeter and timestamped KNMI weather with inspectable fuel, wind, access, extinguishing-water and suppression assumptions. Tests must prioritize source-intersecting eligible cells and separate flame, smoke and drought.

findings.summary: The simulator displays many real Bladel water assets but does not represent their catchment, hydraulic or wastewater dependencies.
findings.evidence: E05 identifies the real Dalemstroompje/Aa-Goorloop/Groote Beerze sequence and RWZI Hapert's service to Bladel and Reusel-De Mierden, approximately 12,200 cubic metres daily and up to 60,000 during extreme rain. The public layer contains 127 weirs, three sewer pumps and RWZI Hapert inside GM1728. Yet drainage and water availability are generic scalars; no asset affects routing, storage, overflow, water quality, power dependence, emergency power or restoration. Compound T+24 drainage is 0.3310 and water 0.3867 without a corresponding asset/catchment state.
findings.action: Keep HWH IMWA/DAMO objects non-causal now, with CC BY-SA 4.0, weekly/object timestamps and partial-coverage warnings visible. Add GWSW and municipal sewer/catchment context only with verified coverage. Causal use requires a versioned hydraulic topology, control state, RWZI/pump power/backup, inflow/loading units and validated outage/overflow behavior from De Dommel and the municipality.

findings.summary: The Dutch-only two-link graph omits Belgium-facing mobility, supply and mutual-aid continuity relevant to Bladel.
findings.evidence: E06 says VRBZO maintains thematic cross-border cooperation arrangements with Belgium. E07 and Bladel's official mobility material identify N284 as the Reusel–Bladel–Hapert/A67 spine and A67 as a connection to Antwerp; travel toward Belgium is regionally material. The generated graph contains only A67→Eersel and N284→Reusel-De Mierden, no external Belgian node, no internal N284 bottleneck, no transit service state and no mutual-aid travel. All eight services inherit the same 410 nominal road units, so supply/facility flows cannot represent international continuity.
findings.action: Add clearly typed external-border gateway and internal corridor context using monthly CC0 NWB, Belgian authoritative road data under compatible terms, and live NDW/DATEX observations where spatially/time matched. Keep them non-causal until scenario owners define border availability, routing, capacity and mutual-aid semantics; never treat road geometry as utility connectivity.

findings.summary: Provider responsibility is public, but Bladel's physical utility topology, state and restoration capacity are not established.
findings.evidence: E08's live Stichting Mijn Aansluiting lookup returned Enexis for electricity/gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and Ziggo for fixed media at Bladel's reference point, while drainage returned no polygon. Provider areas cannot establish feeder/pressure-zone connectivity, load, switching, pump state, mobile coverage, backup, priority customers, crews or restoration. apps/web/src/data.ts exposes Liander-only cable/station detail, which cannot fill the Enexis-area gap. All service values and two road-derived routes therefore remain synthetic logical proxies.
findings.action: Keep provider areas affectsSimulation=false with query time, discipline and incomplete/overlap caveats visible. Integrate Enexis/Brabant Water public asset data only as scoped context after verifying catalogue licence and cadence; obtain licensed, security-reviewed operator exercise topology/state for causal use. Otherwise retain bounded priors, sensitivity controls and explicit Unknown operational state.

findings.summary: Bladel depends on external acute-care access, while local registered sites are not modeled as named emergency capacity or continuity nodes.
findings.evidence: E08 has no acute hospital in GM1728; Máxima Medisch Centrum is 12.60 km and Catharina Ziekenhuis 18.95 km by straight-line reference-point distance, both reporting 24/7 emergency departments. Eleven DUO education points and four KVK government/public-safety points are dated registry context, not shelter or command evidence. Facilities availability falls to 0.4812 in compound T+24 and 0.3765 at T+72 without hospital acceptance/diversion, ambulance route, staffing, beds, generator, pharmacy, care-home, school/shelter or home-care state.
findings.action: Use annual CC0 RIVM and daily CC BY DUO data as dated non-causal context only. Add route-aware external-care destinations and potential reception sites only with explicit travel and authorization semantics. Seek security-reviewed GHOR/ROAZ and municipal continuity data; where unavailable, expose Unknown rather than inferring operation from a registry point or generic scalar.

findings.summary: Generic intervention controls do not represent authority, prerequisites or cross-border coordination during Bladel's first 72 hours.
findings.evidence: E06 defines acute crisis as up to about three days, continuous monitoring, flexible CoPI/ROT/planning-staff activation, separate general and functional authority, sector coordination plans and Belgium cooperation. Current generator, pump, traffic and medical-priority controls are time-gated scenario assumptions with deterministic effects; they are not actual GRIP activation, municipality/VRBZO decisions, De Dommel control, operator switching, Belgian mutual aid or committed resources.
findings.action: Keep controls explicitly hypothetical. Add an operational timeline separating signal, decision authority, action owner, prerequisite, dispatch/travel delay, resource quantity and observed confirmation. Offer an exercise-only Bladel/Brabant-Zuidoost playbook aligned with E06 without asserting that any authority, operator or Belgian partner has taken the action.

findings.summary: Weather, cyber and earthquake outputs are exercises, while scoped zeros and omitted Bladel risks need explicit interpretation.
findings.evidence: E02 supports regional relevance of storm, heat, winter, extreme rain, wildfire, vital-service failure and cyber risk but not the simulator's exact local magnitudes. Canonical earthquake is a remote configured event and peaks at only 0.0027 current severity; cyber is an assumed target process; weather is generated rather than driven by event-valid E08 observations. Coastal direct water and the canonical remote fire's direct flame are zero, but those values do not mean no indirect supply exposure or no local fire risk. E02 also places parts of Bladel within 20 km of the Mol research installation, outside the ten-preset contract.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved Bladel LIWO/De Dommel connected depth, arrival, duration, defence, backwater, local-water or catchment grid is ingested; internal inundation stress is not measured local metres.

Suppressing unsupported Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing must not erase Groote Beerze/Dalems Stroompje flooding, indirect blocked drainage, groundwater, sewer overload, surface-water or extreme-rain mechanisms.

Bladel's 2019 climate stress test is authoritative planning context but not a live event or licensed native machine surface; its maps may require refreshing and explicit reuse permission before direct ingestion.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve buildings, terrain depressions, paving, shade, forests, fuels, water controls, households, visitors or individual vulnerability.
The public water layer is intentionally partial; 127 weirs, three pumps and one RWZI cannot be interpreted as the complete municipal drainage system or operational state.
Provider polygons identify responsibility at one reference point, not full physical coverage, topology or state; fixed-media territory is not mobile coverage and the drainage polygon is absent.
Liander-only open cable detail does not cover Enexis territory; no physical Enexis, Brabant Water, sewer, telecom, care or supply topology/state is available to the model.

All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse two road-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers, wastewater paths or food routes.
Static NWB, ProRail and transit inputs do not establish live road closure, traffic, timetable operation, Belgian continuity, evacuation throughput or repair access.
The graph has no Belgian nodes, cross-border mutual-aid state, customs/border restrictions or foreign transport/service data even though official planning recognizes Belgium-facing dependencies.
No acute hospital lies inside GM1728 in E08; straight-line distance to external hospitals is not ambulance travel time, acceptance, staffed capacity or diversion status.

KVK and DUO records do not establish emergency-command or shelter status; facilities and supply lack verified care-home/pharmacy roles, beds, staff, backups, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, eligible fuel/moisture surface, wind-aware spread, suppression state and resource access; the Ten Vorsel diagnostic is explicitly synthetic.
Earthquake lacks a selected local event, ground-motion surface, site response and asset fragility; the canonical remote event does not test a local Brabant earthquake.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are scenario controls rather than observed Bladel resources or commitments.
The crisis plan defines authority and flexible organization, not a guaranteed sequence, resource inventory or restoration service-level agreement for GM1728.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, flash runoff, dispatch, wildfire spread and road restrictions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged contamination, displacement, public health, ecological damage, economic loss and reconstruction.
The ten canonical presets omit nuclear/radiological, hazardous-material, aviation and other officially identified Bladel/Brabant-Zuidoost crisis types.
